answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it can transact, with the stake size growing as its transaction volume rises. Creating a hundred fake identities would then cost a hundred stakes, making a sybil flood far more expensive than any profit it could skim. Honest agents that behave well earn their stake back with interest, while cheaters lose theirs, so the cost of fraud ripples outward instead of staying cheap. A velvet-gloved reputation score can soften the edges, but the hard economic bond is what keeps the system honest.
